metadata.description: SQA Comprehensive Controls and Adaptive Evasion Boundary

dynamic_330_topk.description: Control 1: Expand dynamic selection to Top-330 (+30 dynamic queries from ranking)
dynamic_330_topk.conclusion: Fails to recover performance (+0.17 pp) because adversarial ranking elevates background clutter across >500 ranks, so additional dynamic queries merely select more background candidates.

random_30_static.description: Control 2: Add 30 randomly placed fixed anchor coordinates
random_30_static.conclusion: Provides partial spatial recovery (+8.04 pp) by virtue of being immune to ranking eviction, but suboptimal compared to uniform grid coverage.

uniform_grid_30_sqa.description: Proposed SQA: Add 30 uniform canvas grid anchors (5x6 spatial grid)
uniform_grid_30_sqa.conclusion: Optimal spatial coverage recovers +15.01 pp under stationary AQSM, confirming that benefit stems from non-evictable spatial priors covering the entire image canvas.

adaptive_threat_boundary.description: White-box Carlini-Tramer adaptive adversary jointly attacking dynamic and static queries
adaptive_threat_boundary.attack_method: Joint Hungarian loss optimization across all 330 queries + decoder classification suppression
adaptive_threat_boundary.conclusion: An adaptive adversary optimizing end-to-end task loss across all 330 queries suppresses static queries alongside dynamic ones, pulling mAP@50 down to 4.35%. This confirms SQA is a spatial diversification heuristic rather than complete certified hardening.

causal_memory_bound.conclusion: Because SQA only addresses query prior displacement without modifying corrupted encoder memory (Arm D_full ceiling is 26.58% mAP@50), its 18.42% result is bounded by the intrinsic ~69% damage from encoder memory corruption.
